title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Auditorium on 1967-11-10
lineage: MR > R > R > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a blistering ’67 show highlighted by a scorching Viola Lee Blues and an all‑out Alligator → Caution marathon.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its pristine, almost modern‑day clarity – a true soundboard source with only a minor glitch around the 8:30 mark in Viola Lee. Musically the band is on fire, delivering powerhouse blues jams (Viola Lee Blues, Good Morning Little School Girl), an epic Alligator → Caution sequence and memorable Pigpen rap moments, all at a consistently high energy level.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 40 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4–5 stars, repeatedly praising both performance and audio fidelity; only a few outlier low‑star comments relate to access issues, not content.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as crystal‑clear, perfect mix with every instrument audible. Some reviewers note a brief glitch in Viola Lee Blues (~8:30) and expected vintage hiss, but these are considered minor or even character‑adding.

standout_songs: Pigpen's Neal Cassady rap (Straight Theatre excerpt)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set opens with a mellow Viola Lee that quickly builds into high‑octane blues, leading into the legendary Alligator → Caution climax; the energy stays elevated throughout with tight transitions and powerful group interplay.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for his fierce guitar tone, blistering solos on Viola Lee Blues, Morning Dew and other jams; described as ‘ripping’ and ‘acid‑voice’ on The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for clear, walking bass lines and occasional solo spots; several reviewers note the excellent audibility of his playing in the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ/harmonica work highlighted as a core element of the show; no specific mention of Keith/Brent/Vince beyond Pigpen’s keyboard contributions.
band_member_comments.Drums: Dual‑drummer chemistry (Bill Kreutzmann & Mickey Hart) especially noted in the Caution jam, with comments on tight yet powerful drumming.
